name: Ribbon Cake
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: 1 teaspoonful saleratus or 3 of baking powder
ingredients.originalText: 1 teaspoonful saleratus or 3 of baking powder
ingredients.quantityText: 1 teaspoonful saleratus or 3 of baking powder

ingredients.name: large cup of raisins stoned and chopped
ingredients.originalText: one large cup of raisins stoned and chopped

ingredients.name: each of cloves and allspice
ingredients.originalText: half a teaspoon each of cloves and allspice

instructions.text: Put half the above in two oblong pans

To the remainder add one tablespoon of molasses, one large cup of raisins stoned and chopped, one teaspoon of cinnamon, half a teaspoon each of cloves and allspice, grate in a little nutmeg, then add one spoonful of flour
Put into two pans of the same size and shape as those above
Put the sheets together while warm, alternately, with a little jelly or raspberry jam between
Cut in thin slices for the table
It will cut most easily the day after it is baked
It may be baked in one large pan without the fruit, pouring in the dark and light in alternate layers
When baked thus it is a handsome marble cake

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put half the above in two oblong pans
2. To the remainder add one tablespoon of molasses, one large cup of raisins stoned and chopped, one teaspoon of cinnamon, half a teaspoon each of cloves and allspice, grate in a little nutmeg, then add one spoonful of flour
3. Put into two pans of the same size and shape as those above
4. Put the sheets together while warm, alternately, with a little jelly or raspberry jam between
5. Cut in thin slices for the table
6. It will cut most easily the day after it is baked
7. It may be baked in one large pan without the fruit, pouring in the dark and light in alternate layers
8. When baked thus it is a handsome marble cake
